paraphrase: Sāṅkṛti asks Dattātreya who the avadhūta is; the name is explained: from imperishability (a), excellence (va), having shaken off (dhūta) the bonds of saṃsāra, and being the meaning of 'that you are' (ta).

original.text: akṣaratvād vareṇyatvād dhūtasaṃsārabandhanāt | tattvamasyādilakṣyatvād avadhūta itīryate

paraphrase: The yogin who has transcended the castes and stages and abides always in the Self is called beyond castes and stages (ativarṇāśramin), the avadhūta.

paraphrase: Or, though his work is done, out of a wish to help the world he may keep to the path taught by scripture — what harm is there to him?

paraphrase: Let the body attend to worship, bathing, cleanliness and alms; let speech repeat the praṇava and read the Upaniṣads; I am the witness, I do nothing and cause nothing to be done.

checks.note: E-text 24-26 located; the passage matches the paraphrase (it begins: 'devārcanasrānaśaucabhikṣādau vartatāṃ vapuḥ | tāraṃ japatu vāktadvatpaṭhatvāmnāyamasta-kam || 24 || viṣṇuṃ…').

paraphrase: 'Blessed am I, blessed am I!' — the knower rejoices that sorrow is gone, ignorance fled, nothing remains to be done or gained.

checks.note: E-text 27-32 located; the passage matches the paraphrase (it begins: 'dhanyo'haṃ dhanyo'hannityaṃ svātmānamañjasā vedmi | dhanyo'haṃ dhanyo'haṃ brahmānando vibhāti mespaṣṭam || 27…').

paraphrase: Bliss is his bird-body — joy its head, delight and great delight its wings, Brahman its support; not by works, offspring or wealth but by renunciation some have reached immortality.

checks.note: E-text 3-5 located; the passage matches the paraphrase (it begins: 'tasya priyaṃśiraḥ kṛtvā modo dakṣiṇapakṣakaḥ | pramoda uttaraḥ pakṣa ānando goṣpadā-yate || 3 ||…').

paraphrase: One who studies this is purified even of the gravest sins; knowing this he may live as he wills.

checks.note: E-text 33 located; the passage matches the paraphrase (it begins: 'itiya idamadhīte so'pi kṛtakṛtyo bhavati | surāpānātpūto bhavati | svarṇasteyā-tpūto bhavati |…').

paraphrase: Moving at will is his wandering; clothed or naked; for him there is no right or wrong in the ordinary sense; desires enter him as rivers the ocean.
